name: Pharmaceuticals and biotechnology
asset: Longitudinal experiments, failed compounds, clinical cohorts and trial infrastructure
mechanism: Use multimodal models and active learning to improve target selection, molecule design and trial stratification. The valuable outcome is more clinically useful candidates per research euro.
capture: Patent-protected products and differentiated clinical outcomes can retain value, but payers and competing treatments can absorb the gain.
kpi: Phase II-to-III transition rate by entry cohort; risk-adjusted pipeline value per R&D euro; time and spend to kill weak programmes
guardrail: No deterioration in toxicity, patient outcomes or trial representativeness
falsifier: More preclinical candidates without improved prospective clinical translation, or costs move into expensive validation
experiment: Compare AI-assisted and conventional programmes matched on modality, therapeutic area, stage and vintage. Include abandoned programmes.

name: Medical devices, diagnostics and surgical platforms
asset: Installed instruments, imaging or procedure data, clinician relationships and service networks
mechanism: AI can improve image reconstruction, diagnostic workflow and procedure planning, allowing each installed system to handle more useful clinical work.
capture: Premium features, service contracts and procedure-linked consumables may capture a share of customer throughput gains.
kpi: Quality-adjusted procedures per installed unit; repeat-scan rate; software attach and renewal rate
guardrail: Sensitivity and specificity by subgroup, adverse events and clinician review time
falsifier: Clinical workflow savings fail to increase billable throughput, or reimbursement falls by the same amount
experiment: Use paired-reader studies and hospital deployment cohorts with equivalent case mix. Separate diagnostic accuracy from billing activity.

name: Life science tools, CROs and laboratory platforms
asset: Instrument footprints, assay protocols, laboratory workflows and trial operations
mechanism: AI can automate experimental design, improve assay yield and shorten trial recruitment or monitoring work.
capture: Consumables, software and workflow switching costs can monetize higher laboratory utilization. CROs must retain savings despite hourly contracts.
kpi: Successful experiments per instrument-day; trial enrollment time; service contribution per project
guardrail: Reproducibility, protocol deviations and trial dropout rates
falsifier: Tools become interchangeable, customer data cannot be reused, or buyers reprice every saved hour
experiment: Compare matched assays or trial sites before and after deployment and account for staffing, protocol and demand differences.

name: Healthcare providers, services and managed care
asset: Care-delivery workflows, appointment capacity and claims or clinical records under restricted rights
mechanism: AI can reduce documentation and scheduling work and improve appropriate care coordination.
capture: Providers may fill scarce clinical capacity. Payers may reduce avoidable cost, subject to medical-loss rules, contracts and consumer protections.
kpi: Clinician time per completed encounter; waiting time; risk-adjusted cost per member
guardrail: Patient outcomes, appeal overturns, denial errors and equitable access
falsifier: Savings depend on inappropriate denials, revenue coding inflation or quality deterioration
experiment: Use controlled clinics or member cohorts, with independent clinical adjudication and case-mix adjustment.

name: Property insurance and reinsurance
asset: Claims histories, exposure records, distribution and underwriting expertise
mechanism: AI can interpret submissions, find fraud and improve risk selection. Reinsurance has sparse tail labels, unlike frequent retail claims.
capture: Better risk selection and lower expense ratios may survive renewals where proprietary information and underwriting discipline persist.
kpi: Accident-year loss ratio adjusted for price and mix; claims expense per resolved claim; new-business risk-adjusted return
guardrail: Reserve adequacy, appeal outcomes, tail concentration and fairness
falsifier: Apparent gains come from reserve releases, a hard pricing cycle, risk exclusion or hidden correlated exposures
experiment: Compare matched underwriting cohorts and claims outcomes. Require a catastrophe-normalized view and adverse development analysis.
horizon: 1–3 years for expense gains; 3–5 for loss emergence

name: Life insurance, wealth and asset management
asset: Policyholder relationships, adviser networks, investment workflows and administrative records
mechanism: AI can improve adviser capacity, policy servicing and client retention. Life underwriting needs long observation periods, while investment research faces crowded signals.
capture: Distribution and recurring administration can retain savings. Investment alpha is a separate, much harder hypothesis.
kpi: Cost per policy or account; adviser assets serviced; persistency or organic net flows
guardrail: Suitability complaints, lapse quality, solvency and performance net of fees
falsifier: Higher adviser output fails to improve net flows, pricing falls, or model portfolios homogenize risk
experiment: Evaluate matched adviser books. Separate market appreciation from flows and separate servicing improvements from claimed investment alpha.

name: Banking and lending
asset: Deposit franchises, transaction histories, credit outcomes and regulated distribution
mechanism: AI can improve fraud controls, service capacity and credit decisions while automating document-heavy operations.
capture: A durable funding franchise and embedded relationships can retain some gains, but competition and credit cycles dominate weak underwriting.
kpi: Cost-to-income at constant business mix; fraud loss per transaction; vintage default and risk-adjusted return
guardrail: Fair lending, model drift, capital use and false credit declines
falsifier: Efficiency gains vanish after provisions or require unsafe automated lending
experiment: Match credit vintages and service cohorts. Hold funding costs and risk appetite constant; separate ML upgrades from interest-rate effects.

name: Payments and transaction networks
asset: Network-level transactions, merchant relationships and fraud outcome signals
mechanism: AI can identify fraud and reduce false declines using context that individual merchants or issuers cannot easily reproduce.
capture: Risk-service fees and higher legitimate transaction volume can monetize improved authorization quality.
kpi: Fraud basis points at fixed approval rate; false declines; net risk-service revenue per client
guardrail: Dispute losses, merchant attrition, rebates and latency
falsifier: Fraud shifts rather than falls, network fees compress, or account-to-account rails bypass the service
experiment: Use randomized or matched authorization policies with equal fraud budgets. Measure issuer and merchant outcomes as well as network revenue.

name: Credit data, exchanges and financial intelligence
asset: Permissioned credit histories, market records, ratings expertise and licensed data feeds
mechanism: AI can turn curated records into underwriting, research and compliance decisions with less manual reconciliation.
capture: Licenses, data entitlements and embedded decision workflows can support paid tools. Public facts alone are a weak moat.
kpi: Paid AI attach; net retention; analyst or onboarding time at fixed error rate
guardrail: Data provenance, model leakage, licensing costs and customer concentration
falsifier: Customers recreate the product with alternative data, or suppliers capture the AI revenue
experiment: Compare incumbent and challenger performance on identical lawful datasets. Then add proprietary features to isolate their marginal value.

name: Legal, tax and professional information
asset: Editorial enrichment, citations, licensed archives and trusted professional workflows
mechanism: AI can convert reference content into validated research, drafting and compliance work.
capture: Paid workflow expansion can exceed lost search seats if customers trust the output and need the underlying content rights.
kpi: Net revenue per customer after seat changes; paid AI renewals; verified task completion cost
guardrail: Citation accuracy, professional liability and content licensing terms
falsifier: Generic agents obtain equivalent trusted answers more cheaply, or seat cannibalization exceeds AI monetization
experiment: Benchmark against generic models and new specialist entrants on blinded jurisdiction-specific tasks, including total human checking time.

name: Vertical software and financial administration
asset: Domain-specific systems of record, transaction context and implementation knowledge
mechanism: AI can perform more bookkeeping, payroll, compliance or industry-specific administration inside the existing workflow.
capture: Outcome or transaction pricing can expand revenue per customer, if seat loss and model costs remain smaller.
kpi: Net revenue per customer; verified tasks completed per support hour; AI contribution margin
guardrail: Reconciliation errors, filing accuracy and human escalation costs
falsifier: Cheaper agents use the system only as a low-price database or customers eliminate more seats than they buy AI services
experiment: Track customer cohorts, usage rights and total bill changes. Include customers that cancel or downgrade.

name: Enterprise systems and workflow orchestration
asset: Business process definitions, permissions, integrations and systems of record
mechanism: AI agents can coordinate transactions across enterprise workflows with existing authorization and audit controls.
capture: Control of execution and compliance may preserve economics even as user interfaces change.
kpi: End-to-end task completion; AI net new contract value; total customer spend after seat changes
guardrail: Rollback success, auditability, inference cost and unauthorized actions
falsifier: A cross-vendor agent captures the interface and forces the incumbent into commodity storage pricing
experiment: Measure completed workflows with customer-level cash cost, including integration and human exception handling.

name: EDA, engineering and design software
asset: Solvers, design-rule knowledge, verified toolchains and workflow integration
mechanism: AI can explore design spaces and generate candidate implementations while deterministic tools validate constraints.
capture: Validated outputs and deep workflow integration can support software pricing or more design volume.
kpi: Engineer hours per verified design; first-pass signoff; paid AI attach
guardrail: Power, performance and area constraints, defects and verification expense
falsifier: Compute and verification costs offset time savings, or customers retain all productivity gains
experiment: Compare designs under identical constraints, compute budgets and signoff criteria. Keep customer IP permissions explicit.

name: Semiconductor fabrication, equipment and process control
asset: Process recipes, yield histories, metrology and installed production equipment
mechanism: AI can improve defect detection, equipment uptime and process-window search.
capture: Leading yields and equipment service value may raise returns. This is separate from selling more capacity to AI customers.
kpi: Yield at equivalent node and product; good dies per tool-hour; unplanned downtime
guardrail: Reliability, node transitions, model drift and customer confidentiality
falsifier: Yield gains reflect product mix or new equipment, while capital intensity and depreciation consume the benefit
experiment: Compare matched tools, wafers and process stages. Account for learning curves that existed before AI deployment.

name: Cloud and diversified technology platforms
asset: Cloud infrastructure, developer ecosystems, distribution and operating datasets
mechanism: AI can improve internal engineering and customer products while platform distribution enables deployment.
capture: Usage revenue and ecosystem control can capture value, but compute investment and model competition can absorb it.
kpi: Cash return on incremental AI infrastructure; cost per completed task; non-AI segment productivity
guardrail: Utilization, depreciation, power availability and internal transfer pricing
falsifier: Revenue grows while cash returns fall, or AI cannibalizes profitable products
experiment: Value cloud, software, advertising and retail separately. Do not count the same AI revenue as both customer savings and supplier profit.

name: IT services, consulting and outsourced processes
asset: Implementation expertise, customer access and operational delivery knowledge
mechanism: AI can reduce the labor required for delivery and increase project throughput.
capture: Fixed-price or outcome contracts can retain savings. Hourly billing may shrink revenue as productivity improves.
kpi: Gross profit per project; revenue and profit per delivery employee; outcome-contract share
guardrail: Rework, utilization, bench costs and client renewal
falsifier: Clients insource using AI, billable hours collapse, or savings are fully passed through at renewal
experiment: Compare contract types and project cohorts, controlling for offshoring, utilization and wage changes.

name: Cybersecurity and identity software
asset: Threat telemetry, endpoint distribution, response workflows and security expertise
mechanism: AI can triage incidents, correlate signals and accelerate response while attackers also use AI.
capture: Trusted security platforms can retain spending if detection quality and integration outperform cheaper bundled tools.
kpi: False positives at fixed detection rate; analyst hours per incident; net retention
guardrail: Missed incidents, adversarial evasion and correlated outage risk
falsifier: Automation adds alert volume, misses novel attacks or cannot offset platform bundling
experiment: Use independent adversarial evaluations and production incident cohorts. Never substitute demo detection for real-world coverage.

name: Industrial automation and electrification
asset: Installed controls, engineering channels, operational telemetry and service expertise
mechanism: AI can improve commissioning, anomaly detection and energy optimization across existing equipment.
capture: Installed-base integration and service contracts may monetize customer downtime savings.
kpi: Commissioning hours; unplanned downtime per operating hour; recurring software attach
guardrail: Safety constraints, latency, uptime and customer data permissions
falsifier: Value requires costly plant-by-plant integration or customers use independent software instead
experiment: Compare similar production cells before staged rollout, controlling for maintenance and capital upgrades.

name: Agricultural, construction and mining machinery
asset: Equipment fleets, dealer networks, field telemetry and work-cycle knowledge
mechanism: Computer vision and autonomy can reduce inputs, operator burden and idle time.
capture: Equipment premiums, subscriptions and services may retain a share of per-acre or per-tonne savings.
kpi: Input cost per acre at equal yield; tonnes per machine-hour; paid software renewals
guardrail: Crop outcomes, incidents, uptime and total retrofit cost
falsifier: Customer savings do not support durable pricing or autonomy needs expensive supervision
experiment: Use paired fields or work sites with equal conditions. Measure whole-season or whole-shift results rather than selected demonstrations.

name: Logistics, parcel, rail and transport networks
asset: Route density, shipment flows, depot networks and asset histories
mechanism: AI can improve routing, load matching, maintenance and network placement.
capture: Dense networks and service reliability can retain savings, although large customers and fuel contracts may demand pass-through.
kpi: Cost per delivered unit at fixed service level; empty miles; asset utilization
guardrail: On-time delivery, damage, overtime and fuel-price effects
falsifier: Rivals deploy identical routing software and bids reset lower, or savings only reflect demand recovery
experiment: Compare matched routes and depots with volume, distance, weather, fuel and service mix held constant.

name: Civil aerospace and long-life equipment services
asset: Certified designs, fleet-service records, engineering expertise and installed engines
mechanism: AI can improve engineering, inspection and predictive maintenance while certification constrains deployment.
capture: Long service relationships and contracted availability can reward lower maintenance cost.
kpi: Unscheduled removals per flight-hour; time on wing; service margin at equal contract mix
guardrail: Flight safety, certification, life-cycle liabilities and inspection misses
falsifier: Predictions fail on rare modes or lower maintenance activity reduces billable revenue
experiment: Evaluate matched fleets by engine variant, utilization and environment. Require independent engineering review.

name: Waste, facilities and route-based business services
asset: Local route density, asset records and recurring commercial contracts
mechanism: AI can improve dispatch, sorting, service planning and customer support.
capture: Density and recurring service relationships can retain some cost savings, especially where local capacity is scarce.
kpi: Cost per stop or tonne; contamination rate; contract contribution margin
guardrail: Safety, service misses, capital costs and labor terms
falsifier: Savings require disproportionate fleet investment or municipal contracts reprice them away
experiment: Compare matched routes and facilities and include replacement capex, training and exception handling.

name: Chemicals, industrial gases and specialty materials
asset: Formulation libraries, application expertise, process plants and customer qualification
mechanism: AI can propose formulations and optimize process conditions, improving experiment throughput and resource intensity.
capture: Qualified formulations, long contracts and application support may retain value. Commodity producers face price pass-through.
kpi: Qualified products per R&D euro; energy per tonne at equal quality; plant uptime
guardrail: Specification failures, scale-up reproducibility and customer qualification time
falsifier: Laboratory improvements fail at production scale or feedstock and pricing overwhelm retained savings
experiment: Use blinded formulation tests and matched production runs. Distinguish specialty pricing from commodity cycle effects.

name: Mining, metals and resource extraction
asset: Orebody knowledge, geological records, equipment fleets and processing plants
mechanism: AI can improve grade control, ore sorting and maintenance, raising recoverable output from existing assets.
capture: Low-cost resource owners may retain operational gains, but commodity prices and royalties remain dominant.
kpi: Recovery at fixed head grade; cost per recovered unit; availability
guardrail: Reserve quality, incidents, ore depletion and sustaining capex
falsifier: Reported gains reflect richer ore or prices, or model output fails at new deposits
experiment: Compare benches and processing runs with mineralogy and grade controls. Separate autonomy from commodity exposure.

name: E-commerce, marketplaces and discretionary retail
asset: Transaction histories, seller networks, customer access and fulfillment or merchandising systems
mechanism: AI can improve matching, inventory allocation and merchandising while reducing seller or service work.
capture: Network density and distribution can capture gains through retention, service fees or advertising. Agents can also bypass storefronts.
kpi: Contribution per order after fulfillment; inventory turns at fixed availability; seller retention
guardrail: Returns, subsidies, customer acquisition and seller economics
falsifier: Agents commoditize discovery, advertising yield deteriorates or savings require permanent discounts
experiment: Run cohort or market tests controlling for subsidies, category mix and fulfillment speed.

name: Mobility, travel and reservation platforms
asset: Demand density, supply relationships, transaction context and booking infrastructure
mechanism: AI can improve matching, itinerary planning and support, increasing utilization and conversion.
capture: Network access and transaction completion may retain value, but external agents can redirect customer relationships.
kpi: Contribution per trip or booking; repeat use; support cost per completed transaction
guardrail: Cancellations, incentives, supplier terms and consumer protections
falsifier: Agents route customers directly to suppliers, commissions fall or autonomy moves bargaining power to fleet owners
experiment: Evaluate matched geographic and customer cohorts. Separate AI conversion from travel cycles and promotional spending.

name: Automotive manufacturers and suppliers
asset: Manufacturing expertise, engineering data, vehicle fleets and service distribution
mechanism: AI can improve design, production quality and service diagnostics. Autonomous driving is a separate capital-intensive thesis.
capture: Brand and differentiated vehicle economics must retain savings despite price competition.
kpi: Warranty cost per comparable vehicle; engineering hours per validated platform; factory yield
guardrail: Recall rates, safety, residual values and software liability
falsifier: Efficiency gains fail to offset price cuts, weak products or loss of geographic competitiveness
experiment: Benchmark matched models and plants. Treat autonomy R&D and commercial manufacturing productivity separately.

name: Consumer brands, apparel and luxury
asset: Brand equity, product archives, direct customer relationships and distribution
mechanism: AI can improve demand forecasting and product iteration while reducing marketing production cost.
capture: Scarce brands and owned customer access may preserve pricing. Generic creative production offers little durable advantage.
kpi: Full-price sell-through; inventory turns; contribution after marketing
guardrail: Brand dilution, returns, discounting and channel conflict
falsifier: Cheaper content increases noise without improving demand or competitors match designs rapidly
experiment: Use product and region cohorts, separating price increases and channel shifts from AI improvements.

name: Food, beverages and household products
asset: Formulation know-how, brands, distribution and manufacturing networks
mechanism: AI can improve formulation, demand planning and plant operations.
capture: Brand strength and efficient distribution may retain part of savings, but retailers and consumers can demand lower prices.
kpi: Waste and energy per unit; launch success by cohort; contribution after trade spend
guardrail: Quality, recalls, promotions and raw-material costs
falsifier: Cost savings simply finance promotions or innovation becomes less differentiated
experiment: Use matched plants and product cohorts controlling for input inflation, mix, pricing and trade spend.

name: Food retail and membership retail
asset: Store networks, inventory flows, purchase histories and customer relationships
mechanism: AI can improve replenishment, reduce spoilage and support store labor productivity.
capture: Scale and repeat purchasing may reinforce advantage, while low-price promises deliberately transfer savings to customers.
kpi: Waste at equal availability; labor hours per basket; member renewal
guardrail: Food safety, service quality, price investment and capex
falsifier: Improved operations produce no durable margin or growth advantage because all savings fund lower prices
experiment: Compare matched stores and fulfillment zones, including labor scheduling quality and basket mix.

name: Telecommunications and connectivity
asset: Network telemetry, spectrum, customer relationships and local infrastructure
mechanism: AI can optimize network energy, fault resolution and service operations.
capture: Network quality and lower cost can improve cash generation, but price competition and regulation may share gains.
kpi: Energy per traffic unit; fault repair time; cash cost per subscriber
guardrail: Dropped calls, outages, churn and traffic growth
falsifier: Traffic or new infrastructure explains improvements, while tariff pressure absorbs savings
experiment: Use staged network-cell deployments and service cohorts, controlling for equipment generation and traffic mix.

name: Advertising, media and entertainment platforms
asset: Audience access, engagement signals, content libraries and recommendation systems
mechanism: AI can improve recommendations and advertiser tools while lowering some production costs.
capture: Distribution and measured outcomes may support monetization, but abundant content can erode creative scarcity and trust.
kpi: Incremental advertiser conversion; retention; contribution after content and compute costs
guardrail: Ad load, privacy, content rights and user satisfaction
falsifier: More engagement does not improve customer value, generic agents bypass discovery or content costs race upward
experiment: Use randomized recommendation and ad tests. Distinguish incremental conversion from attribution changes.

name: Oil, gas and energy services
asset: Subsurface records, engineering workflows, operating assets and customer deployment channels
mechanism: AI can improve reservoir interpretation, drilling decisions and predictive maintenance.
capture: Resource ownership and differentiated services can retain some gains, subject to commodity cycles and contract repricing.
kpi: Nonproductive rig time; recovery or production at fixed geology; cost per unit
guardrail: Safety, emissions, reservoir assumptions and sustaining capex
falsifier: Higher output reflects geology or more investment, or customers capture service productivity
experiment: Compare wells by basin and design and normalize commodity prices and operational exposure.

name: Electric, water and regulated infrastructure utilities
asset: Grid or network telemetry, physical assets and local service obligations
mechanism: AI can improve load forecasting, maintenance and dispatch or leakage management.
capture: Incentive regulation or merchant exposure may retain gains. Allowed returns and rate reviews can transfer them to consumers.
kpi: Outage duration; network losses; controllable operating cost per customer
guardrail: Reliability, affordability, cyber resilience and capital recovery
falsifier: Regulatory resets remove all savings or load growth forces low-return capital spending
experiment: Compare service territories and asset cohorts. Model the actual regulatory sharing mechanism separately from AI load demand.

name: Property ownership, REITs and data centers
asset: Locations, tenant relationships, building systems and operating scale
mechanism: AI can improve maintenance, leasing support and energy management. Data-center rent growth is an AI-demand thesis with different economics.
capture: Lease structure determines who keeps operating savings. Strong locations can support occupancy but do not guarantee an AI moat.
kpi: Same-property NOI at fixed occupancy; owner-retained energy savings; leasing cost
guardrail: Tenant satisfaction, tenant concentration, capex and financing costs
falsifier: Tenants receive all savings or debt and obsolescence overwhelm small operating benefits
experiment: Compare matched properties under identical lease structures. Separate rental market changes from technology effects.

name: Property services and facilities intelligence
asset: Transaction observations, facilities operations and client workflows
mechanism: AI can improve building operations, valuation support and service delivery using property-specific context.
capture: Recurring facilities contracts and workflow integration may retain savings, but client-owned data and fee competition constrain capture.
kpi: Contribution per facilities contract; work-order resolution cost; client renewal
guardrail: Valuation errors, client data rights and service failures
falsifier: Customers internalize the tools or fee cuts fully pass through labor savings
experiment: Use matched managed buildings and service contracts. Separate property transaction cycles from recurring service productivity.
